correctness.rationale: Independence of empty-labelled vertices is precisely an underlying K_n matching M. For t=|M|, the unrestricted selected-edge factor is z^(N-t)(z+2)^(N-t). Absence of a fixed color at k matched edges forces the union of U_k=2k(n-k-1) edge-neighbors to the opposite singleton. Different absent-color families intersect impossibly because two distinct matching edges have four common adjacent K_n edges; same-edge double absence is impossible with nonempty neighbors. Homogeneous-color inclusion-exclusion yields exactly the claimed polynomial. The n>=5 two-part coloring gives a feasible weight N-floor(n/2), and coefficient extraction counts precisely the equality cases. The union bound gives failure fraction at most 2h*2^(-2(n-2)) for a fixed maximum matching. Independently re-enumerated all four-label assignments for n=3,4,5; full coefficient profiles and minimum multiplicities agree; formula evaluated through n=8. Infinite theorem follows from the combinatorial argument, not those finite tests.
residual_risks: The minimum lower bound itself follows from prior vertex-cover reasoning; only the complete polynomial is assessed as new.

value.rationale: The complete named-color weight polynomial is a natural exact invariant of a canonical line/Johnson graph family, not a mere substitution of a known minimum. Matching intersections create genuine two-color dependencies; the formula gives every coefficient, exact optimizer multiplicities, and a quantitative typicality law.
residual_risks: Value is for the complete polynomial; the minimum lower bound alone is an elementary vertex-cover deduction.

limitations: n>=5; no analogous assertion for arbitrary line graphs or unrestricted 2-rainbow labels.
